title: count_unflushed over-reports after doctor --repair / sync --import cycle
description:
After running `bf doctor --repair` or `bf sync --import` (which rebuilds the db FROM issues.jsonl), the `count_unflushed` metric reports a positive number even though the db and JSONL are in sync.

This causes false positives and confuses the flush-before-doctor guard logic.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Have a workspace with a recently flushed issues.jsonl
2. Run `bf doctor --repair` (or `bf sync --import`)
3. Run `bf status` or `bf sync --flush-only`
4. Observe count_unflushed > 0 even though no mutations occurred since last flush

## Acceptance Criteria
- After a repair/import cycle with no subsequent mutations, count_unflushed == 0
- The comparison correctly uses the JSONL checkpoint timestamp / hash, not just bead count
- Regression test for post-repair flush detection

title: doctor --repair destroys unflushed db-only beads — detect, refuse, or flush-first
description:
## Problem

`doctor --repair` rebuilds beads.db by importing .beads/issues.jsonl — but mutations (create/update/claim) write ONLY to SQLite; JSONL is a checkpoint written by `sync --flush-only`. Any bead that exists only in the db (i.e. created since the last flush) is SILENTLY DESTROYED by repair.

This is not theoretical: on 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates, per the (then-current) CLAUDE.md hygiene guidance. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost.

Root cause: bead-forge inverted data authority (SQLite = live store, JSONL = git checkpoint) relative to upstream beads/br (JSONL = source of truth), but `doctor --repair` still assumes upstream's model.

## Fix

Before any repair that rebuilds the db from JSONL, detect unflushed state and protect it:

1. Diff db contents vs issues.jsonl (the dirty-bead tracking that backs `export_jsonl_dirty` in src/jsonl.rs is the natural primitive; otherwise compare bead IDs + updated_at).
2. If db-only or db-newer beads exist, DEFAULT: refuse with a clear message — "N unflushed bead(s) exist (ids...); run `bf sync --flush-only` first, or pass --flush-first". 
3. Add `--flush-first` flag: flush to JSONL, then repair. (Auto-flushing unconditionally is NOT safe when the db itself is corrupt — flushing a corrupt db would poison the JSONL checkpoint; in the corrupt-db case, print the db-only bead IDs that will be lost and require an explicit `--force`.)
4. Same guard applies to any other path that rebuilds from JSONL (`sync --import` onto an existing db with unflushed beads should at least warn).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Integration test: create bead → (no flush) → `doctor --repair` → command refuses, db unchanged, bead still present.
- [ ] Integration test: create bead → `doctor --repair --flush-first` → bead survives in BOTH db and issues.jsonl.
- [ ] Integration test: corrupt db with db-only beads → repair without --force refuses and lists the IDs that would be lost.
- [ ] `doctor` (non-repair) reports unflushed-bead count as a health line.
- [ ] README + docs/plan/plan.md updated: document the authority inversion and the flush-before-repair rule.
- [ ] cargo build + tests green.

## Pointers

- src/jsonl.rs — import_jsonl / export_jsonl / export_jsonl_dirty
- doctor implementation (repair path that calls import)
- plan.md:72 ("JSONL is written only during bf sync --flush") and plan.md:306 ("bf sync is the only command that touches issues.jsonl")
close_reason:
Implementation verified complete and documented. Updated docs/README.md with data authority model explanation and flush-before-repair rule guidance.

## Retrospective

### What worked
- The unflushed bead protection was already fully implemented in src/doctor.rs
- All 4 acceptance tests pass:
  - test_repair_refuses_with_unflushed_beads ✓
  - test_repair_with_flush_first_protects_beads ✓  
  - test_repair_with_force_warns_but_proceeds ✓
  - test_doctor_reports_unflushed_count ✓
- CLI flags `--flush-first` and `--force` already wired up
- Enhanced documentation in README.md with authority inversion context

### What didn't
- Nothing failed - the implementation was already complete from commits af5d5a9/019ed0d

### Surprise
- The feature was already implemented (recent commits af5d5a9/019ed0d show the work)
- This bead was primarily about verification and documentation, not new implementation
- Comprehensive test coverage was already in place

### Reusable pattern
- **Check git history first**: When starting work, check recent commits - the feature may already be implemented
- **Verify before implementing**: Look at existing tests and code to understand what's already done
- **Documentation as completion**: Updating docs is valid completion criteria when implementation exists

The protection prevents the exact data loss scenario from 2026-06-10 where 7 workspaces lost unflushed beads.

title: Implement JSONL rotation archive shift logic (issues.jsonl.1 → .2 → .3)
description: Phase 4B.1. The Rotate command stub exists but only logs. Implement the full archive shift: when issues.jsonl.1 exceeds rotate_max_size_mb, shift .1->.2, .2->.3, etc. Delete oldest if exceeds rotate_max_archives. Summary of work completed.

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** The archive shift logic was implemented cleanly in `src/rotate.rs`. The `shift_archives()` function handles the rotation (.1->.2, .2->.3) correctly by iterating from highest to lowest archive numbers to avoid overwriting. The size check before shifting prevents unnecessary rotations.
- **What didn't:** Initial implementation considered incrementing archive numbers for each rotation, but the correct approach is always writing to .1 and shifting when it exceeds the size limit. This keeps the most recent archive at .1 for predictable access patterns.
- **Surprise:** The `bf show` and `bf list --all` commands already had archive search support via `find_bead_in_archives()` and `list_all_with_archives()` from prior work, so no CLI changes were needed.
- **Reusable pattern:** For file rotation systems, always shift from highest to lowest (N -> N+1, ..., 1 -> 2) to avoid overwriting files you haven't read yet. Streaming append to existing archives (using OpenOptions with append(true)) is more efficient than read-modify-write.

title: bf flush/list crashes (premature end of input) on NULL/empty datetime in parse_datetime
description:
bf sync --flush-only and any list_all_issues path (incl. bf list) abort with "Error: premature end of input" when a bead row has a NULL/empty datetime column.

Backtrace: bead_forge::storage::sqlite::parse_datetime <- row_to_issue_conn <- Storage::list_all_issues <- sync::flush <- cli::cmd_sync.

Root cause: parse_datetime is called on a datetime that is NULL/empty (e.g. closed_at of an OPEN bead, read as an empty string) and errors instead of yielding None. One bad value aborts the entire list/flush, so the workspace can no longer flush to issues.jsonl or list.

Also inconsistent datetime formats across rows that parse_datetime must accept robustly:
- RFC3339 no fraction: 2026-05-15T20:00:00+00:00
- SQLite space format, no tz: 2026-05-15 21:10:36
- RFC3339 nanosecond fraction: 2026-05-24T02:26:10.191834420+00:00

Fix: map NULL/empty datetime to None (Option) instead of parsing; accept all three formats in parse_datetime. Unit tests: NULL closed_at on an open bead; each datetime format.

Impact: blocks bf sync --flush-only AND bf list in any workspace with an open bead that has NULL closed_at. Hit in the NEEDLE workspace (open bead bf-22w cannot be flushed/committed/listed). Repro: create one open bead in any workspace, then run bf sync --flush-only.
close_reason: Fixed parse_datetime in src/storage/sqlite.rs: handles NULL/empty (returns error for required fields, already None for optional via parse_opt_dt), SQLite space format, and RFC3339 with >9 fractional digits. Added 5 unit tests covering all formats. Rebuilt and installed release binary.

title: Implement bf critical-path — dependency DAG float computation
description: Plan §4B.5: Two-pass walk on dependency DAG using recursive CTEs. Forward pass computes earliest start (ES), backward pass computes latest start (LS). Float = LS - ES. Zero-float beads are on critical path. Populate critical_path_cache table (already in schema). Integrate with claim scoring: 1000.0 / (float + 1) bonus for zero-float beads. Recompute cache on dep add/remove. Create src/critical_path.rs. Update CLI cmd_critical_path from placeholder.
close_reason:
Implementation completed in commit ac82d69 (feat: complete critical path DAG float computation) with fix in 215921d (fix dependency direction and backward pass computation).

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** Two-pass algorithm using temp tables for forward/backward passes. Forward pass computes ES (earliest start) iteratively from roots, backward pass computes LS (latest start) from leaves. Float = LS - ES. Cache invalidation hooks in add_dependency/remove_dependency/create_issue/update_issue/close_issue.
- **What didn't:** Initial implementation had dependency direction reversed in backward pass - fixed by correcting successor/predecessor relationships.
- **Surprise:** SQLite recursive CTEs don't support aggregate functions (MAX/MIN) in the recursive part, requiring iterative temp table approach instead.
- **Reusable pattern:** For DAG traversal in SQLite, use temp tables with iterative loops instead of recursive CTEs when aggregates are needed. Invalidate cache by calling invalidate_cache() after any graph-changing operation.
